companies.name: Amazon
companies.summary: Prepare to combine technical problem solving with specific examples of ownership, judgment, and measurable impact.
companies.caveat: The exact sequence varies by team, level, location, and whether an online assessment is used.
companies.rolePathLabel: Build an Amazon SDE II plan

sprint.title: Observable coding
sprint.task: Solve one medium problem while clarifying inputs, narrating tradeoffs, and testing three edge cases.
sprint.evidence: A written solution review with complexity and one correction.

sprint.title: Design under constraints
sprint.task: Design a service from requirements through APIs, data, scale, failure modes, and operations.
sprint.evidence: A one-page architecture with two rejected alternatives.

sprint.title: Leadership evidence
sprint.task: Prepare four concise stories about ownership, disagreement, failure, and customer impact.
sprint.evidence: Each story includes your decision, action, result, and lesson.

sprint.title: Full signal simulation
sprint.task: Run a 60-minute coding-plus-behavioral mock without notes.
sprint.evidence: Three observed gaps and a targeted repeat plan.

companies.name: Meta
companies.summary: Build speed without losing clarity: clean coding, explicit tradeoffs, scalable design, and evidence of impact.
signals: Keep implementation clean under time pressure
companies.caveat: Design format and depth depend strongly on role and seniority; use the recruiter-provided guide as the source of truth.

sprint.title: Fast clean implementation
sprint.task: Complete two timed problems with a strict plan-code-test-retrospective loop.
sprint.evidence: Working code plus a list of avoidable pauses.

sprint.title: Scale the product
sprint.task: Design a feed, messaging, or media workflow and defend data, caching, and reliability decisions.
sprint.evidence: A diagram with bottlenecks and mitigation choices.

sprint.title: Impact narrative
sprint.task: Explain one project from user problem to measurable outcome and your exact contribution.
sprint.evidence: A five-minute recording with no vague team-only claims.

sprint.title: Back-to-back rounds
sprint.task: Simulate coding followed immediately by a design or behavioral round.
sprint.evidence: A rubric score for clarity, correctness, pace, and recovery.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.summary: Show technical depth and a collaborative problem-solving process: assumptions, implementation, testing, design, and learning.
signals: Use concrete examples of growth and collaboration
companies.caveat: Microsoft publishes broad interview guidance; the actual loop is defined by the role and interview team.

sprint.title: Code for maintainability
sprint.task: Solve a problem, then refactor names, boundaries, tests, and error handling as if submitting a review.
sprint.evidence: Before-and-after code with a short review note.

sprint.title: Explain the alternatives
sprint.task: Design one service and compare at least two reasonable approaches before choosing.
sprint.evidence: A tradeoff table tied to requirements.

sprint.title: Growth and collaboration
sprint.task: Prepare examples of feedback, conflict, ambiguity, and learning a new domain.
sprint.evidence: Four stories with specific outcomes.

sprint.title: Collaborative simulation
sprint.task: Practice with an interviewer who changes one requirement halfway through.
sprint.evidence: A note showing how your design and communication adapted.

companies.name: Google
companies.summary: Practice structured problem solving, technical depth, and clear collaboration while staying ready for role-specific variation.
companies.caveat: Google's public guidance is intentionally broad. Do not infer a fixed number or type of rounds without recruiter confirmation.

sprint.title: Structured reasoning
sprint.task: Turn an ambiguous prompt into examples, constraints, candidate approaches, and a justified choice.
sprint.evidence: A solution outline written before code.

sprint.title: Correctness first
sprint.task: Implement and test a data-structures problem, then state the invariant that makes it correct.
sprint.evidence: Code, edge cases, and one-paragraph correctness argument.

sprint.title: Role depth
sprint.task: Choose one role-specific domain and prepare a technical project deep-dive.
sprint.evidence: A diagram plus decisions, failures, and measured results.

sprint.title: Ambiguity simulation
sprint.task: Run a mock where constraints change and follow-up questions increase difficulty.
sprint.evidence: A recovery review: what changed, why, and how quickly.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.summary: Demonstrate exceptional role depth, practical execution, strong collaboration, and thoughtful alignment with the mission.
signals: Show deep evidence in the target discipline
Explain how you move from ambiguity to delivery
Discuss safety and judgment where relevant
Bring thoughtful questions about the work
companies.caveat: Assessment format varies significantly by role; the official guide and recruiter communication should override generalized preparation.

sprint.title: Exceptional role depth
sprint.task: Select the hardest relevant project and explain the underlying technical decisions at increasing levels of detail.
sprint.evidence: A ten-minute deep-dive with source artifacts.

sprint.title: Build under ambiguity
sprint.task: Complete a small role-relevant work sample with explicit assumptions, tests, and limitations.
sprint.evidence: A runnable artifact and decision log.

sprint.title: Judgment and mission
sprint.task: Prepare examples where quality, safety, speed, and user value created real tension.
sprint.evidence: Three evidence-backed decision stories.

sprint.title: Technical challenge defense
sprint.task: Present your work sample, receive adversarial questions, and revise one weak decision.
sprint.evidence: A post-review change with rationale.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.summary: Prepare for technically rigorous, mission-aware conversations that reward clear thinking, practical skill, and honest uncertainty.
signals: Use evidence instead of confident guessing
Show relevant implementation or research depth
Explain why the mission and role fit
companies.caveat: Public careers information changes as roles evolve; confirm the current loop and allowed tools with the recruiting team.

sprint.title: Reason under uncertainty
sprint.task: Analyze a technical claim with incomplete evidence and state what you know, infer, and still need to test.
sprint.evidence: A calibrated decision memo.

sprint.title: Role-specific technical depth
sprint.task: Implement or analyze one task representative of the target role without hiding uncertainty.
sprint.evidence: A reproducible artifact and evaluation notes.

sprint.title: Mission connection
sprint.task: Connect your past choices to responsible AI development without generic enthusiasm.
sprint.evidence: Two specific stories and three thoughtful questions.

sprint.title: Evidence-first simulation
sprint.task: Run a mock where every confident claim can be challenged with 'what evidence supports that?'
sprint.evidence: A list of unsupported claims you corrected.
